builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: StateMirror: Pre-Execution Detection of Hallucinated Tool Calls in Coding Agents
summary: StateMirror replaces reactive, post-execution failure feedback and LLM-judge detection with a deterministic pre-execution validator that checks action predicates against the live repository at the harness boundary. It costs only the engineering effort to integrate AST and command analysis into the agent loop; it adds negligible runtime overhead (1.50ms) and zero token cost. It can fail on the roughly 18% of hallucinations it misses (F1 0.817), on environment states not expressible as static predicates, and on dynamically generated or highly dynamic codebases where AST extraction is incomplete.
rationale: It requires no GPU, no model training, and no tokens, and directly reduces token spend and wall-clock time for any team running LLM coding agents in production.
technique: Pre-execution hallucination detector for coding agents

claims.statement: StateMirror replaces reactive, post-execution failure feedback and LLM-judge detection with a deterministic pre-execution validator that checks action predicates against the live repository at the harness boundary. It costs only the engineering effort to integrate AST and command analysis into the agent loop; it adds negligible runtime overhead (1.50ms) and zero token cost. It can fail on the roughly 18% of hallucinations it misses (F1 0.817), on environment states not expressible as static predicates, and on dynamically generated or highly dynamic codebases where AST extraction is incomplete.

StateMirror achieves 0.940 precision and 0.817 F1, reduces median detection latency from 17.73s to 1.50ms with zero token consumption, and in live mitigation reduces agent execution time by 15.8% and token consumption by 11.8%.
